subject: Chemistry
q: According to the Hardy–Schulze rule, which is the correct order of flocculation values for the listed electrolytes when coagulating positively charged ferric hydroxide sol?
hint: For a positive sol, compare the valencies of the anions; flocculation value is inverse to coagulating power.
solution: Ferric hydroxide sol is positively charged, so the active coagulating ions are anions. Their valencies are 3− for [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, 2− for CrO₄²⁻, and 1− for Br⁻, NO₃⁻ and Cl⁻. Higher counter-ion valency means greater coagulating power and therefore a lower flocculation value. Hence K₃[Fe(CN)₆] < K₂CrO₄ < KBr = KNO₃ = AlCl₃.
